findings.numbers: 1.4B with 4 text + 4 image experts, 1T tokens: 3.7x FLOPs savings overall (2.6x text, 5.2x image); a mixed 8-expert MoE gives 3x
findings.implication: Supports the FAB_MOD_GROUPS arm (hard modality expert blocks) against purely learned routing.

findings.claim: Mixture-of-Transformers gives each modality its own non-embedding parameters (FFN, attention, norms) while keeping global self-attention over the whole sequence.
findings.source: Liang et al. 2025, arXiv:2411.04996 (TMLR 2025); abstract via search
findings.numbers: Chameleon-7B setting: matches dense with 55.8% of FLOPs; adding speech: comparable with 37.2% of FLOPs
findings.implication: Modality-specific parameters inside a shared sequence are cheap. New modalities can get new parameters instead of overwriting shared ones, which also serves B.

findings.claim: The Byte Latent Transformer groups bytes into dynamic patches by next-byte entropy. It matches tokenizer-based LLMs at scale and improves inference efficiency, robustness, reasoning and long-tail generalisation.
findings.source: Pagnoni et al. 2024, 'Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens', arXiv:2412.09871 (ACL 2025); abstract via search
findings.numbers: FLOP-controlled scaling study up to 8B parameters and 4T training bytes
findings.implication: A byte substrate with learned segmentation is scale-proven. The tree's byte-level online BPE is on the door-opening path, and entropy patching is an alternative lever.

findings.claim: bGPT predicts the next byte, and matches specialised models across text, audio and images. It also simulates algorithms and hardware.
findings.source: Wu et al. 2024, 'Beyond Language Models: Byte Models are Digital World Simulators', arXiv:2402.19155; abstract via search
findings.numbers: ABC-to-MIDI conversion at 0.0011 bits/byte error; CPU simulation accuracy >99.99%
findings.implication: Bytes can be the universal interface to any digital modality, which keeps A's doors open without a codec per modality.

findings.claim: Byte-level models process any language out of the box, are more robust to noise and do better on spelling- and pronunciation-sensitive tasks. Parameter-matched, they are competitive with subword models.
findings.source: Xue et al. 2022, 'ByT5', arXiv:2105.13626 (TACL 2022); abstract via search
findings.numbers: competitive with mT5 at matched parameters; better on noisy text
findings.implication: The byte substrate serves both A (universality) and the unreliability theme (noise robustness).

findings.claim: ImageBind learns one joint embedding across six modalities (images, text, audio, depth, thermal, IMU) using only image-paired data. Alignment between modalities never observed together emerges.
findings.source: Girdhar et al. 2023, arXiv:2305.05665 (CVPR 2023); abstract via search
findings.numbers: six modalities
findings.implication: A hub modality binds new modalities without all pairwise data. For the tree, text is the natural hub, consistent with 'B first, A later'.

findings.claim: A transformer pretrained on language, with its self-attention and feed-forward layers frozen, transfers to numerical computation, vision and protein fold prediction, gaining performance and compute efficiency.
findings.source: Lu, Grover, Abbeel, Mordatch 2022, 'Pretrained Transformers as Universal Computation Engines', arXiv:2103.05247 (AAAI 2022); via search
findings.numbers: qualitative
findings.implication: A good text core is itself a door to other modalities. This supports the owner's ordering: B first, A added later onto the core.

findings.claim: Representations in different models, including vision and language models, become more aligned as they scale (position paper).
findings.source: Huh et al. 2024, 'The Platonic Representation Hypothesis', arXiv:2405.07987 (ICML 2024 position); abstract via search
findings.numbers: qualitative
findings.implication: Weak support that a shared latent space across modalities becomes easier with scale. A hypothesis, not a result.

findings.claim: Flamingo bridges frozen pretrained vision-only and language-only models and handles arbitrarily interleaved images, video and text. The new cross-attention layers are gated with tanh gates initialised at zero, so the frozen LM is unchanged at the start and keeps its text ability.
findings.source: Alayrac et al. 2022, arXiv:2204.14198 (NeurIPS 2022). The bridging claim is from the abstract via search; the zero-init gate detail comes only from secondary sources
findings.numbers: gate initialised to 0 (secondary)
findings.implication: Zero-born gated pathways are how a modality is added without disturbing the core. 03 already lists this as an isolation arm. Confirm the gate detail in the PDF.

findings.claim: Lifelong-MoE adds experts (and gating dimensions) for each new data distribution, freezes the old experts and gates, and regularises to preserve knowledge. Compute stays constant.
findings.source: Chen et al. 2023, 'Lifelong Language Pretraining with Distribution-Specialized Experts', arXiv:2305.12281 (ICML 2023); abstract via search
findings.numbers: better few-shot results on 19 downstream NLP tasks than earlier lifelong methods
findings.implication: Growing experts and freezing old ones is the MoE form of 'add capacity, don't overwrite'. It maps onto FAB growth plus protection of old experts (FAB_COMP_PROTECT).

findings.claim: Branch-Train-MiX branches a seed model, trains domain experts in parallel, mixes their FFNs as MoE experts, averages the other parameters, then fine-tunes the MoE to learn token-level routing.
findings.source: Sukhbaatar et al. 2024, arXiv:2403.07816; abstract via search
findings.numbers: generalises Branch-Train-Merge and sparse upcycling
findings.implication: New skills or modalities can be trained in isolation and merged later, which bounds interference while they are being learned.

findings.claim: Expert Gate adds one expert per task and routes each test sample by which task's autoencoder reconstructs it best. It needs no stored data from earlier tasks.
findings.source: Aljundi, Chakravarty, Tuytelaars 2017, arXiv:1611.06194 (CVPR 2017); via search
findings.numbers: qualitative
findings.implication: Reconstruction-error novelty is an old, working router for adding tasks. The tree has analogues (FAB_AE_W, MEM_VERIFY='recon').

findings.claim: Progressive networks add a new column for each task, with lateral connections to earlier columns. They are immune to forgetting and reuse earlier features.
findings.source: Rusu et al. 2016, 'Progressive Neural Networks', arXiv:1606.04671; abstract via search
findings.numbers: Atari and 3D maze tasks
findings.implication: This is the limit case of freeze and add: zero forgetting at the cost of growth. It bounds what FAB growth can promise.

findings.claim: Almost every multimodal LLM evaluated fails to keep its vision encoder's image-classification performance. Continued fine-tuning of LLaVA helps at first, then causes hallucination and loss of generalisation, even with the image encoder frozen.
findings.source: Zhai et al. 2023, 'Investigating the Catastrophic Forgetting in Multimodal Large Language Models' (EMT), arXiv:2309.10313; abstract via search
findings.numbers: qualitative
findings.implication: Naive fine-tuning to add a modality damages both sides. Adding modalities needs replay, gates or isolation, which is the evidence behind 03 section 9's rehearsed default.

findings.claim: MERA (merge, then realign) extends multimodal LLMs to new modalities almost without loss, with no heavy parameter budget and no architecture change.
findings.source: MERA 2025, 'Merge then Realign: Simple and Effective Modality-Incremental Continual Learning for Multimodal LLMs', arXiv:2503.07663 (EMNLP 2025); abstract via search
findings.numbers: 99.84% average Backward Relative Gain when extending to four modalities
findings.implication: Adding modalities one at a time can be close to lossless with simple machinery. That supports the owner's 'with B, we can add A later'.

findings.claim: A hypernetwork trained to predict embeddings for any tokenizer transfers encoder and decoder LLMs to new tokenizers, coming close to the original on cross-lingual and coding tasks.
findings.source: Minixhofer, Ponti, Vulic 2024, 'Zero-Shot Tokenizer Transfer', arXiv:2405.07883 (NeurIPS 2024); abstract via search
findings.numbers: remaining gap closed by continued training on <1B tokens; tested on XLM-R and Mistral-7B
findings.implication: A tokenizer is not a closed door. The tree's live vocabulary with anchored new rows (LM_ANCHOR_W) belongs to the same family.

findings.claim: In-tree: when a modality is added as a new area, replay keeps text nearly unchanged, while pure-add forgets heavily. WORLD forgets about 3x the LM's amount under pure-add.
findings.source: LLM-Test docs/proposals/03_AUDIO_VIDEO.md section 9 (Route 1 and Route 3 prototypes); read this session
findings.numbers: tree GRU+WORLD: pure-add 2.966 -> 3.196 bits/token (+7.8%), 30% replay 2.966 -> 2.906; masked pure-add 1.936 -> 7.846 bits/byte vs 25% replay 1.936 -> 1.931; WORLD text MSE 1.02 -> 3.21 pure-add vs 1.10 with replay
findings.implication: In-tree confirmation at toy scale that 'modality = area + replay' keeps A's door open without breaking B. Per-module (WORLD) forgetting must be reported separately or it hides.

lit.belief_assessment:
THE HYPOTHESIS: "the challenges of an unreliable system will force it to generalize." The literature breaks it into four claims. They have different evidence and hold in different regimes. Honour the belief in the forms where evidence supports it, and test it where it does not.

(1) INVARIANCE. Training under a perturbation P makes the model robust to P. STRONGLY SUPPORTED, but only for the same family of perturbation.
- For:
  - BPE-dropout: up to +2.3 BLEU.
  - Subword regularisation: best in low-resource and out-of-domain settings.
  - Domain randomisation: a detector accurate to 1.5 cm in the real world, trained only on simulated images.
  - Noisy Student: ImageNet-C mCE 45.7 -> 28.3.
  - In-tree: source-tag dropout of 0.25 gives an untagged read of 1.585 / 1.656 / 1.317 bits/byte, against 2.246 / 2.214 / 2.064 with no dropout.
- Limit: robustness does not carry to a perturbation not trained on. Nets trained on salt-and-pepper noise are not robust to uniform noise (Geirhos 2018). CLIP's robustness comes from the diversity of its training distribution, not from noise (Fang 2022).

(2) REGULARISATION. Injected noise improves CLEAN held-out generalisation. DEPENDS ON THE REGIME.
- It helps when data is scarce or repeated:
  - dropout;
  - NEFTune: AlpacaEval 29.79% -> 64.69% in small-data instruction tuning;
  - stochastic depth: a 1202-layer ResNet reaches 4.91% on CIFAR-10.
- It hurts in data-rich, single-pass LM pretraining. Liu, Bauer and Manning 2025: at Pythia 160M and 1.4B, no dropout beats both dropout and early dropout on LM, BLiMP, SQuAD and MNLI.
- Consequence here: at RUN_EPOCHS 1 on a fresh stream, the literature predicts LM_DROPOUT or TOK_DROPOUT > 0 costs clean bits/byte. After training, replay repeats data, which moves toward the regime where noise helps. So the verdict can flip between phases: an argument for a lever that is scheduled by phase, not for a constant.

(3) ADAPTATION. Variability in the MAPPING itself (what a symbol means, what the dynamics are) forces in-context or memory-based adaptation. SUPPORTED ABOVE A THRESHOLD.
- Automatic domain randomisation produced emergent meta-learning in memory-augmented policies (OpenAI 2019).
- In-context learning emerges from bursty data, many rare classes and dynamic item meanings (Chan 2022).
- A task-diversity threshold separates reproducing the pretraining prior from a general solution (Raventos 2023).
- Meta-learners pass from instance memorisation to task identification to general learning as model size and task count grow, limited by state and memory size (Kirsch 2022).
- Below the threshold, the same variability is memorised.
- This form has the best evidence of the four. It ties unreliability to memory and context (MEM, LM_CTX), not only to weights.

(4) TOLERANCE OF UNRELIABLE CONTENT (wrong targets, junk, liars, poison). CONTRADICTED unless the model can attribute what it sees to a source.
- Nets fit random labels and even pure noise, and explicit regularisation does not change this (Zhang 2017).
- With symmetric label noise, accuracy is a quadratic function of the noise ratio (Chen 2019).
- Label noise produces double descent, and in some regimes 4x more data hurts (Nakkiran 2020).
- Junk data sharply cuts knowledge capacity (Allen-Zhu and Li; the "about 20x at 7/8 junk" figure is from a secondary summary). A domain tag restores it.
- About 250 poisoned documents backdoor models from 600M to 13B, whatever the amount of clean data (Souly 2025).
- Training on the model's own outputs collapses the tails of the distribution unless real data is accumulated alongside (Shumailov 2024; Gerstgrasser 2024).
- Tolerance can be bought, but with data: over 90% on MNIST at 100 noisy labels per clean one needs proportionally more data and larger batches (Rolnick 2017).
- In-tree:
  - credibility did not emerge inside the model without a tag;
  - learning-progress focus without trust drew more from the liar than from the credible source at 4 of 5 seeds (0.179-0.221 vs 0.123-0.135);
  - a live, drifting codec gave no consistent gain on codec-invariant readings (caption bits/byte worse at 11 of 16; understanding exact worse at 5 of 8).
- Also against the belief:
  - adversarial robustness trades against clean accuracy (Tsipras 2019);
  - competition between modalities is tied to instability (Aghajanyan 2023).

NET. The belief holds as "benign, zero-mean stochasticity of inputs and representations, plus variability of mappings, with memory and source identity available". It does not hold for unreliable targets, or for sources that cannot be attributed. There the evidence contradicts it, and it collides with B's bound on risk. The practical line:
- unreliable INPUTS and SEGMENTATION: lever, arm, schedule by phase;
- unreliable MAPPINGS: build them into areas and read adaptation;
- unreliable SOURCES and TARGETS: attribute with tags, gate with trust, never trust by exposure alone.

RULINGS THAT LEAN ON THE BELIEF:
- TOK_DROPOUT and the live retokenisation cadence (TOK_RETOK_EVERY);
- LM_DROPOUT;
- DATA_TAG_DROP;
- live codec drift (03b);
- FAB_MUT and FAB_BIRTH_JITTER;
- noise areas and liar sources in the self-regulation testbed;
- any self-regulated noise controller.

TEST IN THIS TREE (owed; pre-register). An unreliability ladder, the "U-series".

Families:
- (a) segmentation: TOK_DROPOUT and retok cadence;
- (b) representation: LM_DROPOUT;
- (c) cue: DATA_TAG_DROP;
- (d) codec drift rate;
- (e) mapping variability: a synthetic "dynamic meaning" area whose key-to-value map changes per segment;
- (f) content: liar-source share and noise-area share;
- (g) targets: a fraction of corrupted continuations.

Design: levels 0 / low / mid / high; 5 paired seeds; matched on tokens and compute. Run two regimes: single-pass, and replay with repeated data.

Readings:
- R1: clean held-out bits/byte per area.
- R2: held-out under the SAME family.
- R3: held-out under a family NOT trained on (leave one family out). This is the decisive reading for "forces generalization".
- R4: continual metrics: forgetting (BWT), depth of the stability gap, and a plasticity probe (bits/byte after N windows on a brand-new area).
- R5: in-context adaptation on the dynamic-meaning area, and MEM hit rate.

Predictions from the literature:
- R1: an inverted U for (a)-(c) in the replay regime; a monotone cost in single-pass.
- R2: improves for every family.
- R3: near zero, unless several families are mixed.
- R4/R5: (e) helps above a diversity threshold.
- (f) and (g): monotone harm without tags or trust; less harm with tags.

Verdict:
- The strong form is FALSIFIED if no family at any level improves R1 or R3 beyond the spread of paired seeds while R2 improves. That result means invariance to the seen noise only.
- It is SUPPORTED if a mixed-family arm improves R3 and R4 at equal compute.
- An ADR-style arm, which raises the noise level automatically while held-out loss stays within tolerance, is the self-regulated version the owner would prefer. The plain ladder is its control.

Measurements that exist (all toy scale, all signals):
- tag dropout: supports the invariance form;
- live codec: inconclusive or against;
- self-regulation liar results: against tolerance without attribution.

Owed: the U-series itself, the leave-one-family-out reading, and the plasticity probe.
lit.safe_post_training_learning:
PRINCIPLE. Send each kind of new information to the cheapest reversible channel that can hold it. Promote it toward the weights only through gates. Keep an untouched anchor to roll back to. The evidence ranks the channels as follows.

T0: TEMPORARY WEIGHT UPDATES (test-time training, dynamic evaluation; updates discarded or per-episode). No lasting risk.
- Test-time training: up to 6x for small models; 53% on the ARC public validation set, 61.9% with program synthesis. It needs prior fine-tuning on similar tasks, augmentations and per-instance training (Akyurek 2024).
- Training on 20 retrieved neighbours, one step each, narrows a 10x size gap (Hardt and Sun 2024).
- Dynamic evaluation: Transformer-XL on enwik8 goes from 0.99 to 0.94 bits/char (Krause).
- Not in the tree. Owed: an evaluation-time adaptation lever with reset.

T1: MEMORY (kNN-LM, RETRO, GRACE; the tree's MEM). Low risk: every write is local, auditable, and deletable per entry or per source.
- kNN-LM: 15.79 perplexity on WikiText-103, 2.9 points better, with no training. It adapts to a domain by swapping the datastore.
- RETRO: comparable to GPT-3 on the Pile with 25x fewer parameters.
- GRACE: thousands of sequential edits with no weight change.
- RAG beats unsupervised fine-tuning for both new and existing knowledge (Ovadia 2024).
- In-tree caveat: in the one real continual run, every English memory entry was evicted during the Python phases. Memory contributed -0.111 b/B; retention came from weights (+0.052 drift, held) and the fabric (+0.373). Memory is therefore the lowest-risk WRITE channel here, but not yet a demonstrated RETENTION channel.
- Owed: a phased run with per-source floors (MEM_SRC_SHARE) and eviction that spares faded sources, reporting memory's contribution per area.

T2: SPARSE OR SLOT WEIGHT UPDATES (memory layers, adapters, new experts). Moderate risk.
- Sparse memory fine-tuning: NaturalQuestions F1 drops 11%, against 89% for full fine-tuning and 71% for LoRA, at equal new learning (Lin 2025).
- LoRA learns less and forgets less; full fine-tuning's perturbations are 10-100x higher rank (Biderman 2024).
- Lifelong-MoE adds experts and freezes the old experts and gates.
- Tree analogues: FAB slots, growth and protected culls; anchored new vocabulary rows.
- Limit: forgetting still grows as a power law in parameters touched and in steps (Kalajdzievski 2024). Sparse updates slow forgetting; they do not prevent it.

T3: DENSE CONSOLIDATION (the LM core). Highest risk, so it runs in gated consolidation phases.
What works:
- Replay plus LR re-warm and re-decay matches full re-training at 405M and 10B (Ibrahim 2024). The rate is about 5% for a weak shift and about 25% for a strong one (secondary figures).
- Replay also raises target-data efficiency, up to 1.87x (Kotha and Liang 2026).
- Spaced, per-example replay recovers 5-37 points of old knowledge and beats uniform replay at scale (SRT 2026).
- In-tree, 25-30% replay makes adding a modality nearly lossless: 1.936 -> 1.931 bits/byte, against 7.846 for pure-add.
- Keep updates close in KL to the anchor. Forgetting is predicted by the KL between the new and base model on the new task, and on-policy updates forget less (RL's Razor 2025).
- Stability-gap mitigations for LLMs: replay a mixture like the pretraining data, and use several epochs on a smaller high-quality subset (Guo 2024).

SCHEDULE. Learning after training needs a schedule with no end date. Four options have evidence:
- constant LR plus cooldown tracks cosine (Hagele 2024; the repo cools down over 20% of training);
- WSD needs no step count set in advance (MiniCPM);
- infinite schedules beat repeated cosine, because every re-warm causes forgetting (Singh 2025);
- schedule-free needs no stopping time but still needs tuning (beta 0.95-0.98 on long runs).
MoE LLMs continually pretrained with replay and an infinite schedule match re-training, and their routers stay balanced (Therien 2025).
CONFLICT: the tree's default is cosine with restarts, fitted to a known run length (OPT_LR_SCHED='cosine', OPT_LR_RESTARTS=True).

PLASTICITY. It must be maintained, not assumed.
- Plasticity loss is measured in GPT-style LMs from 5M to 314M parameters; its onset grows sublinearly with size (2026).
- Standard networks decay to the learning ability of a shallow network (Dohare, Nature 2024).
Remedies with evidence:
- weight decay plus layer normalisation (Lyle 2024);
- L2 toward the initial weights (Kumar);
- shrink-and-perturb (Ash and Adams);
- continual backprop, or resets paired with replay (Dohare; Nikishin);
- larger pretraining weight decay, which improves later adaptability (Han 2026);
- gradual rather than abrupt shifts (Liu and Mou 2026).
CONFLICT: OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY=0.0 by default.

GATES.
- A fixed, disjoint held-out probe per area, read continuously with worst-case metrics. Every common continual-learning method dips when a shift starts and then recovers: the stability gap (De Lange 2023; Guo 2024). A gate with no recovery window rejects good updates. A gate that reads only at phase ends misses the damage.
- Negative-flip rate per probe (Yan 2021).
- KL to the anchor on a fixed reference set.
- A plasticity probe.
- Canary and trigger probes for backdoors.

ROLLBACK.
- Rotating checkpoints: CKPT_BEST_KEEP exists but defaults to 0; it should be ON for B.
- Graded rollback by interpolating weights toward the anchor: WiSE-FT gains 4-6 points under shift at no cost.
- Memory deletion by source.
- NOT gradient unlearning: 10 unrelated examples recover most "unlearned" capability (Lucki 2024).
- NOT locate-and-edit: ROME and MEMIT edits end in collapse at scale (Gupta 2024).

TRUST AND POISONING. Poisoning depends on a count of documents, not a fraction:
- about 250 documents, across 600M-13B models and 6B-260B tokens (Souly 2025);
- 0.1% persists through SFT and DPO; denial-of-service works from 0.001% (Zhang 2024);
- 100 examples poison instruction tuning, and filtering gives only moderate protection (Wan 2023);
- backdoors survive SFT, RL and adversarial training (Hubinger 2024);
- 0.01% of LAION could be poisoned for $60 (Carlini);
- Tay, which learned from open input, was corrupted within 16 hours.
Therefore:
- provenance tags on everything that is learned;
- per-source rate limits and caps on both memory writes and share of weight updates (dilution does not work against a fixed-count attack);
- quarantine new content in memory; promote it to weights only after independent corroboration and a delay;
- partition influence by source (DPA-style certificates exist for classifiers; for LMs this is unmeasured);
- self-generated data is tagged and accumulated alongside real data, never substituted for it;
- self-regulated focus must be gated by trust, because learning-progress focus is exactly what a noisy or lying source exploits (in-tree: the liar was amplified at 4 of 5 seeds).

NOT ENOUGH ON ITS OWN:
- EWC-style regularisers (the stability gap remains);
- dropout (does not stop plasticity loss);
- weight editing (collapses at scale);
- filtering alone.

MEASUREMENTS.
- Exist in the tree, toy scale: replay on modality addition; the one phased continual run; the self-regulation retention probe.
- Owed:
  - the schedule arms (cosine with restarts vs constant+cooldown vs WSD vs infinite) under equal replay, read on cooled branches;
  - a weight-decay / L2-init arm read on the plasticity probe;
  - a probe gate with a recovery window vs no gate, counting false rollbacks;
  - poisoning canaries with per-source caps on and off;
  - memory's retention contribution with source floors on.
lit.universality:
WHAT KEEPS DOORS OPEN

1. A byte substrate with learned segmentation.
- Byte models are more robust to noise and to spelling-sensitive tasks (ByT5).
- Next-byte prediction matches specialist models on text, audio and images (bGPT): 0.0011 bits/byte converting ABC notation to MIDI, and over 99.99% accuracy simulating a CPU.
- The Byte Latent Transformer, with entropy-based patches, matches tokenizer-based LLMs FLOP for FLOP, up to 8B parameters and 4T bytes.
- Tokenizers are not a closed door either:
  - a hypernetwork moves a model to a new tokenizer, with less than 1B tokens to close the remaining gap (ZeTT);
  - instruction-tuned models keep 93.4% of their performance under random non-canonical tokenisations (Broken Tokens).
- The tree's byte-level online BPE, with live retokenisation and anchored new rows, is on this path.

2. One shared sequence (early fusion).
- Gato puts 604 tasks into one flat token stream with one set of weights (about 1.2B parameters).
- Unified-IO 2 handles images, text, audio and action in one model.
- Chameleon and Emu3 train a single transformer on discrete mixed-modal tokens.
- Perceiver IO handles arbitrary input and output arrays at linear cost.
- At equal compute, early and late fusion reach similar loss, and early fusion is better at small parameter counts (Shukor 2025, 457 models).

3. Modality-aware sparse capacity inside the shared sequence.
- MoMa (4 text + 4 image experts, 1.4B, 1T tokens): 3.7x fewer FLOPs than dense overall; 2.6x for text, 5.2x for images.
- Mixture-of-Transformers matches Chameleon-7B with 55.8% of the FLOPs, and speech with 37.2%.
- MoE learns modality-specific weights (Shukor).
- In the tree: FAB with the hard modality-group arm (FAB_MOD_GROUPS) against learned routing. This also serves B: a new modality gets new parameters instead of overwriting shared ones.

4. A continuous path beside the discrete one.
- Transfusion scales significantly better than discrete image tokens, and compresses images to 16 patches with modality-specific encode and decode layers.
- Emu3 argues the opposite at its scale.
- Keep both as levers. The table vs coordinate rows in 03/03b are the tree's local version of this choice.

5. A hub that binds the others.
- ImageBind binds six modalities using only image-paired data.
- A transformer pretrained on language and then frozen transfers to numerical, vision and protein tasks (FPT).
- A position paper argues representations converge across modalities as models scale (the Platonic hypothesis).
- Text as the hub fits the owner's order: B first, A later.

6. Stabilisers for mixed streams.
- Competition between modalities comes with instability at small scale; synergy appears only with scale (Aghajanyan 2023: 8M-30B parameters, 7 modalities).
- Chameleon needed QK-norm, reordered normalisation and z-loss (details from secondary sources).
- Unified-IO 2 needed 2D RoPE, QK-norm and dynamic packing.

ADDING MODALITIES OR TASKS WITHOUT FORGETTING. What has worked:
- Freeze the core and bridge to it, with new gated pathways born at zero (Flamingo; the gate detail comes from secondary sources).
- Add experts and freeze the old ones (Lifelong-MoE). Progressive networks add a column per task and are "immune to forgetting", at the cost of growth.
- Train branches in isolation, then mix them as MoE experts and learn the router (BTX).
- Route by which task's autoencoder reconstructs the input best (Expert Gate).
- Merge then realign: 99.84% backward relative gain across four added modalities (MERA 2025).
- Plain replay. In the tree, 25% replay keeps text at 1.936 -> 1.931 bits/byte, where pure-add goes to 7.846.
Known failure: fine-tuning an MLLM first helps, then causes hallucination and loss of generalisation, even with the image encoder frozen (EMT).

WHAT CLOSES DOORS
- (i) An LR schedule tied to a known run length. It rules out learning after training. The tree has this by default.
- (ii) Vocabularies, embedding tables or output heads sized or typed for one modality.
- (iii) A discrete-only media path, with a frozen codec as the only interface. Transfusion suggests a quality ceiling; 03b documents the codec's own drift trade-offs.
- (iv) Positional structure that is 1-D only, for 2-D or temporal media.
- (v) A dense core where every new modality must overwrite shared weights: competition at small scale.
- (vi) Discarding raw data or codec inputs, which rules out later replay and re-encoding.
- (vii) Routing tables that fix the set of modalities, with no path to spawn a new one.
In the tree, (ii)-(vii) are mostly avoided by design (LM_VOCAB_SLOTS, FAB growth, area-based modality addition, DOM spawn). (iii) is an open lever. (i) is a live conflict.

SCALE CAVEAT. The evidence on forgetting versus scale conflicts:
- Luo 2023: forgetting grows from 1B to 7B in continual instruction tuning.
- Ibrahim 2024, per a secondary summary: 10B forgets less than 405M in continual pretraining.
Competition between modalities turns into synergy only at scale. Toy-scale verdicts about A are signals and can invert.

MEASUREMENTS.
- Exist in the tree, toy scale: replay when adding a modality (03 section 9); live vs frozen codec (03b).
- Owed:
  - FAB_MOD_GROUPS against learned routing on a mixed stream;
  - a continuous-input path against codec tokens at equal compute;
  - a modality-purity reading of DOM domains (03 M2);
  - WORLD forgetting reported per area.

rulings.ruling:

- R-CKPT absent-field rule:

rulings.why_A: Transport blocks keep media out of the BPE id space. The reserved IMG index and the per-block layout leave room for more modalities. Adding VID or IMG moves no stored id.

With the freeze stamp gone and OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM 0, nothing adjusts the LR at media arrival. Meanwhile the LM schedule is cosine fitted to the run length (OPT_LR_SCHED='cosine', OPT_LR_RESTARTS=True), so late arrivals meet a decayed rate.

rulings.ruling:
Run the owner's GPU sweep on the combination split: LM width 128/256/512 x media seconds per epoch 600/3,000/15,000, fresh clips. Add two axes the framing requires.
- (1) Combination DIVERSITY:
  - widen aud/tones' attribute values so the number of trained combinations grows (about 32 -> 100 -> 300), with the held-out combinations and the seconds fixed.
- (2) A U-series mixed-perturbation arm:
  - segmentation noise plus codec drift plus tag drop, together;
  - read on held-out combinations (the leave-out reading R3).
Attribution rule:
- if width moves composition, it is scale;
- if the diversity axis moves it at fixed width, it is variety;
- if neither does, go to the architectural arms (continuous insert; WORLD rollout with the free-running loss).
Report per attribute, with at least 100 held-out-combination prompts per area. Before the GPU sweep, pilot the diversity axis in the design-world harness on CPU at 1-2 seeds.

rulings.flexibility: Every axis is a DATA lever: DATA_MEDIA_HOLD_COMBOS, generator variety, perturbation levers.
rulings.unreliability_belief:
This is the design's clearest test of the belief.
- For: the literature's form (3), variability of mappings above a task-diversity threshold, produces general solutions (Raventos 2023; Kirsch 2022).
- Against: every route and arm is at 0-15% on held-out combinations, including the one at 0.94 in-distribution.
- Falsified (strong form) if the mixed arm improves same-family robustness while held-out-combination exact does not beat the paired-seed spread at any width.
rulings.risk: No direct risk to B; the cost is GPU hours. Guard: pre-register the attribution rule.

rulings.ruling:
A perceptual metric trained from scratch is allowed for EVALUATION, as a frozen measurement instrument.
- Train it once per real area on held-out data, version it, and never update it during a run it measures.
- Never make it a training loss of the model it evaluates.
- Pretrained metrics stay excluded.
- It is the gate reading for real media after training, next to the synthetic canary probe families (03b-16.18), because DATA.recover returns None for real areas.
- A training-loss use of a SEPARATE, independently trained instance may exist only as an off arm, and only after real data exists. The analytic 'multires' loss is the first-line fix for timbre.
rulings.why_B: Live adaptation of the codec to real audio after training needs a gate. Without this metric, real-media learning is unguarded.
rulings.why_A: Real audio quality needs a reading beyond synthetic recover exact.
rulings.flexibility: The off-arm route keeps a learned loss possible without letting it grade itself.
rulings.unreliability_belief: Not relevant. An unreliable instrument is not the belief's 'unreliable system': instruments must stay fixed.
rulings.risk: The learned probe is fragile: 2.3% on reconstructions before augmentation. It can make a gate fire falsely or miss. Guard: the synthetic canaries stay primary, and the metric reports its own calibration against recover exact.
conflicts_noticed: 'Nothing frozen' vs an instrument frozen per measurement: 03b scopes measurement contracts out of the rule.
03b-16.18: the guard relies on recover exact, which exists only for synthetic data.

FAB owns the per-modality running baselines (a state_dict key, a restore row, a geometry note), and DOM receives a copy as an argument. As 03b amends R11:

The 8 kHz grid vs real-audio fidelity for A.

rulings.ruling:

- AUD_REHEARSE 0.5; AUD_REWARM 0.

- Arms: the 1/4 cadence, anchor 0, jit_ema, high plasticity, the frozen control.

- Evidence: live vs frozen showed no consistent LM-side cost or gain (caption worse 11/16, understanding worse 5/8, generation better 18/32) and a consistent codec-ceiling cost (7/8).
- So there is no support yet that drift forces generalisation, and no refutation.
- Falsifier: an LM trained on the live codec, read on a held-out perturbed codec (R3), is no better than an LM trained on a frozen codec.

- The anchor evidence leans against it: recover exact is lower in 5 of 6 readings.

'Nothing frozen' vs the frozen control.

rulings.ruling:

rulings.ruling:

Add under B:

- (2) An OFF arm for hold expiry pulls the live codec back toward the held snapshot by weight interpolation (WiSE-FT style), instead of adopting a codec still beyond threshold.
- The default stays 'refresh with a warning' (the no-hidden-freeze rule) until S3/S5 show which bounds risk better.

rulings.ruling:
Build 'replay' at SR0 (DATA_REPLAY_SHARE 0.27, DATA_REPLAY_NEWEST 0.0) and 'retention' at SR2, both OFF. E1 still decides, with four changes fixed before it runs.

(1) Keep the primary endpoint (all-area end-state held-out bits/byte, 32 windows, 5 paired seeds, one-sided paired t at alpha 0.05).
(2) Add a B guard that any default candidate must pass: per-area non-inferiority against the best hand-set arm. The arm must not be significantly worse (one-sided paired t, alpha 0.05) on any area, and no area may be worse by more than a margin of 0.05 bits/byte (the toy's minimum detectable effect), fixed in advance.
(3) Add the time-integrated all-area gap as the first tie-breaker, ahead of Q2.
(4) Add a continuation shape (e), which is the 'after training' test. Each shape-(b) end checkpoint resumes as a child on a real area absent from the parent's schedule, for 25% of the parent's windows. Arms: planned / replay / replay_newest / retention, with DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT True for the rehearsing arms. That is 20 runs.
(5) On focusbed, 'retention' is eligible only if noise_outdraws.P3 is 0 and the liar's drawn share is at most the credible source's at 4 of 5 seeds.
(6) Run E1 at the LR schedule the OPT ruling adopts, and run E2 before E1.

Interim default: 'planned' stays until SR0 builds 'replay'. After that, 'replay' 0.27 is the default appropriate for B. It changes only runs that have faded areas. Flipping it is the owner's call; E1 can overturn it.
rulings.changed_from_current:
Changed.
- Adds a worst-area guard, a time-integrated tie-breaker, a continuation shape (e), a trust-gating eligibility condition, a schedule dependency, and E2-before-E1 sequencing.
- Names 'replay' as the interim default appropriate for B once built; the doc keeps 'planned' until E1.
- Why: under B the end-state mean alone is the wrong single endpoint, and on the toy the choice of endpoint flips the verdict. My paired recomputation of the doc's numbers gives:
  - end-state focus - m27: t -0.81 (tie);
  - time-integrated: t -4.05 (retention better);
  - worst areas: easy +0.076, t 3.24; cred +0.137, t 4.90 (retention worse).
rulings.why_B:
- 'planned' is the only draw that forgets catastrophically: easy forget 0.9-1.9 bits against under 0.05 with either rehearsing draw.
- At the shipped 4-area schedule, derive.phase_schedule gives [[eng,py],[py,num],[py,num],[num,c]]. So eng is unprotected for 75% of the run, and a child under 'planned' has no rehearsal at all.
- The replay-over-planned evidence is the strongest in the study: -0.178 to -0.317 at 5 of 5 seeds, t -10.8, reproduced. It agrees with 03 §9 (25-30% replay gives 1.936 -> 1.931 against 7.846 pure-add) and with the literature's tier T3.
- In deployment every moment is an end state. So anytime (time-integrated) performance and worst-area risk are B's real endpoints, and the continuation shape is the only arm that measures learning after the main run.
rulings.why_A:
- Draws are defined over areas, so they are modality-agnostic.
- A fixed 0.27 split evenly shrinks per area as areas multiply: at 20 faded areas each gets 1.35%. 'retention' spends where need is measured, which scales to many areas or modalities.
rulings.flexibility:
- 'retention' sets the rehearsal amount from measured forgetting. The literature's replay fraction depends on shift size (about 5% for a weak shift, about 25% for a strong one), and a fixed 0.27 is a number fitted to one toy's realised rho, the same pattern as a run-length-fitted LR schedule.
- At the shipped 2-live shape, its flexibility is mostly rho sitting at its 0.3 cap (rho_at_cap P3 0.53-0.96). The shape (e) and focusbed arms are where flexibility can show.
rulings.unreliability_belief:
- Weakly relevant as a benefit: a varying mixture is not the mapping variability that belief form (3) needs.
- Directly relevant as a hazard (form 4). Learning-progress focus without trust drew the liar more than cred at 4 of 5 seeds (0.179-0.221 against 0.123-0.135). Noise out-drew both credible sources in P3 at 5 of 5. Unreliable content exploits self-regulation, hence eligibility condition (5).
rulings.risk:
- **'retention' starves slow-progress areas** (easy, cred, corrob all significantly worse than m27). Guard: the per-area guard.
- **Act machinery.** 'retention' adds redraw events, a FAB blackout of up to 54%, and resume risk. Guard: SR1's resume test.
- **Flipping to 'replay' breaks pairing** with runs that have faded areas. Guard: pending fleets pin DATA_DRAW='planned'.
- **E1 is judged under a decayed cosine schedule**, where selection gains may vanish (No Train No Gain). Guard: condition (6).
rulings.decisive_test:
- **E1, owed, owner GPU.** 75 runs plus 25 for shape (d) plus 20 for shape (e). The guard and the time-integrated gap are computed from the same runs.
- **CPU precursors, owed:**
  - SR0's 'replay' realisation and PYTHONHASHSEED tests;
  - SR2's P3 interference known answer at 3 seeds on focusbed.
- **Existing toy evidence:** rev/metrics.txt, judge/compare.txt, repro/ns.txt, and the recomputation in scratch paired.py.
conflicts_noticed: 'Performance decides' vs the standing preference for self-regulation (Q2).

The instrument line: 'retention' turns a held-out reading into a training decision on one run. eval/levers.py:146-148 calls this 'the one direction the instrument line otherwise forbids', and PLAN 3.8 forbids a verdict on n=1. Proposal 04 never mentions it. The owner should rule that in-run control decisions are logged, reversible controls, not reported verdicts.
The E1 verdict depends on the OPT schedule ruling. OPT_LR_SCHED='cosine' with OPT_LR_RESTARTS=True is fitted to the run length, a door the B literature flags. This dependency is not in depends_on.
E1/E2 ordering: E1 judges 'retention' at internals E2 has not honed (REHEARSE_EVEN 0, FLOOR 0.3), while E2's rule reads E1's endpoint.
The endpoint choice flips the toy verdict: tie on end state, win on time-integrated, loss on the worst area.
A 'tie' at 5 seeds means |diff| below about 0.053 bits/byte at the toy's variance. It is not equivalence.
Q4: shape (e) needs DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT.

rulings.changed_from_current: Changed from an unconditional 'yes' to 'yes, if it is safe, cheaper in risk and really self-regulating'. B's bounded-risk requirement and the doc's own finding that only rho is regulated at the shipped shape both argue against a blind tie-break.
rulings.why_B:
- A tie in the mean with worse tails is not neutral for B: bounded risk is about the worst area.
- After training, the shift size and the arrival pattern are unknown. A rehearsal amount set by the run's own measurement generalises to shifts the toy never had. That is a B reason to break a genuine tie toward 'retention', but only when the controller actually moves.
rulings.why_A: Hand-set shares do not scale to many areas or modalities. Breaking ties toward the self-regulating arm keeps that door open.
rulings.flexibility: Flexibility is the tie-breaker here, conditioned on flexibility actually being exercised (condition (c)), not just built.
rulings.unreliability_belief: Not directly relevant. The trust-gating eligibility in Q1 condition (5) must already hold before any tie-break applies.
rulings.risk:
- **Shipping 'retention' on a tie** buys 4.3%+ wall, act and resume complexity, and FAB blackout for no measured gain. Guard: conditions (a)-(d).
- **The opposite error:** shipping 'replay' locks in a number fitted to one toy's rho. That is acceptable because 'retention' stays built, so nothing is removed.
rulings.decisive_test:
- No measurement decides a preference. The conditions are read from E1 (owed, owner GPU).
- The B-specific evidence would be 'retention' beating 'replay' at the continuation shape (e) while tying at (b).
conflicts_noticed: 'Performance decides' vs 'self-regulation for a large part'. Only the owner can rank them, and the conditions narrow the conflict to genuine, safe ties.
'Never remove functionality' is not violated either way: both arms stay built.

rulings.ruling:
Yes: build DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT (bool, default False; levers 306). Areas that are in DATA_AREAS and in the parent's record, and live in no phase of the child, count as faded from window 0 under 'replay' or 'retention'. Under 'planned' it does nothing.

Pure-add stays the unprotected-forgetting control of the add-an-area test: arm P, per the Q-DATA-7 resolution. The continuation or post-training protocol (E1 shape (e), and any deployment-style child run) sets it True.

Three arms: P (pure), P+parent (True), R (rehearsed sliding window). The child must find the parent's area bodies on disk. It refuses loudly if they are missing, and never degrades silently.
rulings.changed_from_current: Changed. The doc says 'no by default; build only if the owner says yes'. Under B I recommend building it, because it is the mechanism that protects learning after the main run. The default stays False, so pure-add keeps its meaning and the owner's 'keep pure add as the add-a-domain protocol' ruling is honoured.
rulings.why_A: 'B first, add A later' literally means adding modalities as new areas after training. This lever lets that addition keep what the parent knew.
rulings.flexibility: The post-training path becomes a per-run choice. Under 'retention', the child decides from measured need how much of the parent to rehearse.
rulings.unreliability_belief:
- Pure-add is the harsh, unprotected condition. The belief could predict that the fabric learns to protect under it.
- The one measurement (+0.444 pure against +0.046 rehearsed) is against that at toy scale.
- P against P+parent is a direct test: does FAB preserve without rehearsal?
rulings.risk:
- **Parent data is absent at child time.** Guard: a loud refusal and a counter.
- **A silent change to pure-add's meaning.** Guard: the default False, and Plan.protocol still recognises pure_add.
- **Retention-probe rows for parent areas must persist across the run boundary.** They do: holdout_probe is keyed by area name.
rulings.decisive_test:
- **Owed:** Q-DATA-7's measurable pair extended by the P+parent arm, read on eng's held-out block across the run boundary, 3-5 paired seeds. It can run on CPU at toy shape; at owner shape it runs on GPU as E1 shape (e).
- **Existing:** Q-DATA-7 toy pair (1 seed); 03 §9.
conflicts_noticed: The owner's 2026-09-02 ruling keeps pure-add as the default protocol of the add-a-domain test. Default False honours it, but availability is the owner's call.
'Discarding raw data closes doors' (literature): the policy must keep the parent's area data for rehearsal.

rulings.flexibility: Plumbing. The lever keeps OFF available.

rulings.ruling:
Build DATA_REHEARSE_EVEN, with 0.0 as the build default ('retention' is OFF, so it changes nothing at shipped defaults). E2 tests 0.0 against 0.5 and runs before E1.

E2's rule for this lever changes to B's risk rule: 0.5 is adopted if it lowers the worst faded area's end-state gap at 3 of 3 seeds and the all-area mean is not significantly worse (one-sided paired t, alpha 0.05). If E2 cannot separate them, E1's 'retention' arm carries 0.5, the risk-bounding value. The measured value 0 has a significant worst-area regression against fixed replay.
rulings.changed_from_current:
Changed.
- The decision rule moves from mean-endpoint to worst-area.
- An unresolved E2 carries 0.5 into E1.
- E2 runs before E1.
- Evidence: easy is worse than m27 under need-only splitting (+0.103 / +0.048 / +0.117 / -0.003 / +0.117; mean +0.076, t 3.24), with P3 shares 0.079-0.119 against 0.135.
rulings.why_B: 'Without risking too much' means the slowest-forgetting old area must not be starved. A need-weighted split gives slow forgetters a small share even though their end state is worse.
rulings.why_A: With many faded areas or modalities, a need-only split concentrates rehearsal on the fastest forgetter. An even floor spreads it.
rulings.flexibility: 0.5 halves the self-regulated part of the rehearsal split. Flexibility is traded for bounded risk, stated openly. The split's need-driven half remains.
rulings.risk:
- 0.5 dilutes rehearsal toward areas that do not need it, which may erode hard's end-state advantage (mean -0.104, not significant). Guard: E2 reads hard's gap too.
- With 3 seeds, power is low. Guard: the tie goes to the guard value, not to the untested one.
rulings.decisive_test:
- **E2, owed, owner GPU:** 3 paired seeds, shapes (a) and (b).
- **CPU pre-check, owed:** the d3 testbed with a small scratch patch adding an even floor, 5 seeds (a few minutes per run on CPU).
conflicts_noticed: The E1/E2 ordering in depends_on is reversed: E1 should judge the honed 'retention'.
'Self-regulation for a large part' vs a hand-set floor. This is a guard, as the doc already classes floors.

If E2 is unresolved, 0.5 goes into E1's 'retention' arm.

Per-area gaps are always reported beside per-phase byte shares. Trust-weighted allocation ('loss+draw') is the value-aware route, but it stays OFF until E5 and SR6.

rulings.ruling:

- Everything stays in observe until:

  - E3's audit (100 sampled conflicted claims per rule, dominated by content, not boilerplate);

- 'ctx' floored a truthful different-format source (r 0.001, t 0.3) and trusted the liar (r 0.999) at 2 of 2 seeds (critic/out/td_fmt_cred_K5_*). Actuating that would be a B hazard.

- 'kv' does not close a door, since it is a lever value, but it is not universal. The MEM-key aligner is the universal-capable path.

rulings.unreliability_belief: Form (4) is contradicted without attribution. Claim-level agreement is the attribution machinery that makes unreliable sources survivable.

- **E5:** owed, owner GPU.

DATA may not import TOK, so 'kv' key normalisation needs a root-composed decode callable (O10).

rulings.ruling:
Keep full-tail acts, rate-limited (DATA_FOCUS_ACT_EVERY 6 probes, DATA_FOCUS_SHIFT_TV 0.1, zero-TV acts refused), for training runs built on S0b. Revisit if E2's TOK.splice timing on the 17 MB tail exceeds +10% wall.

Three B-driven additions:
(1) Build a bounded look-ahead draw as a lever value, OFF: DATA_DRAW_HORIZON in windows, where 0 means the whole epoch (the default). It lays only the next K windows, with each chunk logged as a seg_log event so resume stays bit-exact. Build it after SR2. Learning after training consumes an open-ended stream that cannot be laid up front.
(2) Unify the stamp counters: fab.blackout_windows (04) and fab.cooldown_windows (03b) become one counter, and E2 measures the combined share with 03b's stamps on.
(3) Build the stamp scope as a lever, DATA_FOCUS_STAMP 'all' (default) / 'opt'. If the combined blackout exceeds 20% of windows, redraw-only acts stamp OPT only. 03b's stamps alone are 20-27% by arithmetic, so expect the rule to trip.
rulings.changed_from_current:
Changed.
- Adds the look-ahead draw as a built-OFF lever; the doc only records it as an alternative.
- Adds counter unification, and makes the stamp scope a lever decided on the combined 03b + 04 share.
rulings.why_B:
- FAB growth is B's sparse-capacity channel for new material. Blacking it out for more than 20% of windows (54% worst case with 04 alone) blocks it.
- 'The whole epoch up front' assumes a known run length, the same door-closing family as a run-length-fitted LR schedule and OPT.revise_horizon. Learning after training needs a draw that works on an unknown-length stream.
rulings.why_A: New modalities or areas arrive at arbitrary times. A look-ahead draw absorbs arrivals without a full-tail re-lay.
rulings.flexibility: A look-ahead draw can respond every K windows without whole-tail splices. The stamp scope becomes testable instead of fixed.
rulings.unreliability_belief: Weak. Retok acts perturb segmentation (U-series family (a)); redraw-only acts do not move the view.
rulings.risk:
- **Look-ahead turns the startup exposure Gate into a projection** and needs per-chunk rng children. Guard: chunk events in seg_log and a resume test like SR1's.
- **Not stamping FAB on redraws** can let growth fire on a self-caused mixture shift (the CAP runaway precedent, 2048 -> 8192 in 19 lifts). Guard: read fab.grown_* around redraw acts.
rulings.decisive_test:
- **TOK.splice timing on a 17 MB tail:** owed (also S0b measurement 3). It is a timing, not training, so it is runnable on CPU here.
- **Combined blackout share with FAB on:** owed, owner GPU (E2).
- **Look-ahead against full-tail equivalence** (the same shares give the same realised bytes within one segment): owed, CPU.
conflicts_noticed: S0b's 'whole epoch up front' design vs an open-ended post-training stream.
03b's act stamps compound with 04's; the same gauge has two names (fab.blackout_windows vs fab.cooldown_windows) and exists in neither src.
OPT.revise_horizon and the LR schedule assume a known length; this depends on the OPT schedule ruling.

rulings.ruling:
- Build OPT_DAMP_SOURCE: 'off' is the default, 'probe' an arm.
- The probe must hand OPT a Reading with value = the mean probe bits/byte over every seen area and seed_count = 1. It must not be a bare float: OPT._reading raises a ValueError on a bare float (opt/api.py:540-561).
- At seed_count 1, OPT refuses to damp under PLAN 3.8 and counts opt.restart.damp_refused_n1. The arm therefore makes the counters declared UNREACHABLE reachable telemetry (how often damping would have fired), but it does not damp.
- Whether an in-run control decision is a 'verdict' under PLAN 3.8 is an owner ruling.
- The more important use under B: make the same reading the producer of CKPT.Retention.consider's curve_bpb, the best-checkpoint rollback anchor. compose.py:1663-1675 says 'Saves.best can never be non-zero' for the same missing producers (units_by_domain, logits_fn) that 04's two root joins supply. It takes effect when CKPT_BEST_KEEP > 0, whose default belongs to the rollback ruling.
rulings.changed_from_current:
Changed.
1. A Reading carrying seed_count, not 'the mean probe bits/byte'.
2. The doc's 'makes an existing self-regulator reachable' is only half true: at n=1 OPT refuses to damp.

rulings.group_notes:
Cross-cutting findings for the self_regulation group. No training was run. The paired statistics were recomputed from the preserved JSONs by /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/dec/rule_self_regulation/paired.py.

1. **The endpoint decides the verdict under B.** On the toy, 'retention' (focus) against fixed replay (m27), paired over 5 seeds:
   - end-state mean6 ties: -0.014, t -0.81;
   - the time-integrated gap favours retention: -0.055, t -4.05;
   - the worst areas go against it: easy +0.076 (t 3.24), cred +0.137 (t 4.90), corrob +0.175.
   B needs anytime performance and bounded worst-area risk, so E1's pre-registration should add a per-area non-inferiority guard and a time-integrated tie-breaker. At the toy's variance, a 'tie' over 5 paired seeds means |diff| below about 0.053 bits/byte. It is not equivalence.

2. **'planned' is B's riskiest draw.** The shipped 4-area schedule is [[eng,py],[py,num],[py,num],[num,c]] (derive.phase_schedule), so eng is unprotected for 75% of the run. Evidence that replay beats planned: 5 of 5 seeds, t -10.8, the in-tree 03 §9 result, and the literature. Once SR0 builds it, 'replay' 0.27 is the interim default appropriate for B. The flip is the owner's call, and E1 can overturn it.

3. **The instrument line and PLAN 3.8, unaddressed by 04.**
   - 'retention' and OPT damping both turn a held-out reading into a training decision on one run.
   - OPT refuses a bare float and refuses to damp at seed_count 1. So Q10 as written would either raise or never damp.
   - In-run self-regulation is n=1 by construction. The owner should rule that in-run control decisions are logged, reversible controls, while PLAN 3.8 continues to govern reported verdicts.

4. **The probe's producers also unblock rollback.** 04's two root joins (units_by_domain, logits_fn) are the same producers CKPT.Retention.consider lacks (compose.py:1663-1675: 'Saves.best can never be non-zero'). The probe should feed CKPT's curve_bpb, the rollback anchor B needs, and not only OPT.

5. **Dependencies missing from depends_on:**
   - the E1/E2 verdicts depend on the OPT schedule ruling (cosine with restarts, fitted to the run length) and on weight decay;
   - E2 should run before E1, so E1 judges the honed 'retention';
   - FAB_LR_OWN depends on the schedule ruling and on the P1-H15 crash fix.

6. **Trust must gate self-regulation.** Learning-progress focus amplified the liar at 4 of 5 seeds, and noise out-drew both credible sources in P3 at 5 of 5. Before 'retention' can be a default, it must pass focusbed known answers for the liar and noise. Poisoning is count-based, so a per-source count cap (DATA_SRC_CAP, OFF) is recommended beside the agreement-based book.

7. **Correction to the literature digest.** It says tag dropout 0.25 gives 1.32-1.66 bits/byte untagged against 2.06-2.25 without dropout, but that mixes forget_easy with untagged mean6. Like for like (d2/out), the untagged mean6 gap is:
   - drop 0.25: 1.736 / 1.757 / 1.670;
   - drop 0: 2.246 / 2.214 / 2.064;
   - never tagged: 1.751 / 1.665 / 1.621.
   So there is same-family invariance but no gain in clean generalisation (+0.051, t 2.56, worse), which is the falsification pattern of the belief's strong form for one family at toy scale. It also means E4's own rule, applied to the toy, keeps DATA_TAG OFF.

8. **B-native gaps found:**
   - DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT should be built: it is the only path that protects learning after the main run.
   - A bounded look-ahead draw should be built OFF: the whole epoch laid up front assumes a known length.
   - DATA_REHEARSE_MAX, the de facto rehearsal amount (binding in 53-96% of re-plans), is missing from E2 and from the doc's 'unmeasured' list.
   - fab.blackout_windows (04) and fab.cooldown_windows (03b) name the same gauge, which exists in neither src.
   - 03b's stamps alone are 20-27% by arithmetic, so Q9's 20% rule is likely to trip.

9. **Pending fleets.** The S0b retok fleet and the WORLD re-test do not need strict before/after sequencing if they pin DATA_SYNTH_HOLDOUT=0, EVAL_RETENTION_EVERY=0 and DATA_TRUST='off' (and DATA_DRAW='planned' if flipped). SR0 and SR3's bit-identity tests make that pin exact.

(2) The shipped cadence is PROVISIONAL until the re-run 03b already promises on held-out per-area bits/byte (04 SR0's EVAL.holdout_probe) passes the same rule on the WORST area. B's risk is worst-case, not mean. (3) Secondary readings are reported beside the rule, not in it: per-area prequential; stability-gap depth over the 200 windows after each act; fab.cooldown_windows (arithmetic: FAB_COOLDOWN 400 blacks out growth for 40% of windows at k1000 and 13% at k3000); tok.mint_wait_windows; MEM remap share; splice timing on a 17 MB tail. rulings.why_B: The act is the only path by which minted ids reach training data at RUN_EPOCHS=1. At 0, about 594 mints per 20k-window run stay stranded (99 bursts x 6), so the tokenizer is frozen in-run. After training, a new domain's new ids would never enter the stream. The cadence is in absolute windows, so it carries into an open-ended life with no run end. The risk is bounded: acts are logged; resume is bit-exact (c8d8e33, tests/test_continuation.py S5); a no-op act is refused; the lever reverts.
rulings.why_A: Byte-level online BPE with live re-segmentation is the universal-substrate path (BLT, ByT5). The same act carries AUD refresh and the media relay. Even if 0 ships, the act still serves AUD and resume, so A's door stays open in either outcome.
rulings.flexibility: The firing cadence is the flexible option, and the rule already gives ties to it (non-inferior means it ships). That matches the owner's tie-to-flexibility and self-regulation preference.

rulings.ruling: The default stays 0, and the record is corrected. OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM is an ATTENUATION: _schedule multiplies the cycle by max(min_frac, ramp) (opt/api.py:468-473), so it can only LOWER the rate and then ramp back. It is not the literature's re-warm (Ibrahim; Gupta 2023), which RAISES the rate back to a maximum. It therefore cannot supply post-training plasticity, and it cannot solve 03's R13 (media arriving on a decayed LR). At the floor it would drop the rate to min_frac squared, 0.25% of peak, for no B benefit. Keep it as a stability-gap guard arm: N in {0, 100, 400} steps, where 400 equals FAB_COOLDOWN so OPT and FAB pause together. Measure it at S0b acts, at S5 media arrival, and at the add-an-area resume. The upward re-warm that B and 'add A later' actually need is ruled under FRAME-POST-TRAINING as a continuation schedule.

rulings.ruling:
Define learning after training as a NAMED PROTOCOL: 'continue', recognised and named on the Sample the way Q-DATA-7 (c) recognises protocols, not a mode switch that computes other levers (the L1 defect). It is a resume of a parent checkpoint onto an open stream, launched by a script that sets explicit levers. The protocol itself is OFF unless launched. Its components, each behind its own lever, with defaults stated:

(1) SCHEDULE WITH NO END DATE (owed build). Add OPT_LR_SCHED choice 'plateau'. At the resume it ramps from the parent's current rate to OPT_LR_PLATEAU x peak over OPT_LR_CONT_WARM steps (default 1000, the tree's warmup), then holds. Cooldowns run only on BRANCH children used for evaluation and serving, never on the learner (the WSD / infinite-schedule pattern). Provisional plateau 0.25 x peak; arms 0.05 (today's floor behaviour with a log) and 1.0 (Ibrahim). Not 1.0 by default, because a constant 2e-3 is exactly the regime in which all 17 old pilots turned upward after about 6000 steps (Q-OPT-3). The main-run OPT_LR_SCHED stays 'cosine', because every record was taken at cosine, until the schedule arms run. A non-inferior 'wsd' main-run arm wins ties because it serves B.

(2) REPLAY ON. Build 04 Q4's DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT (default False, keeping the D2 and 04 measurement semantics). The continue protocol sets it True, at 0.27-0.3 of bytes from the parent's areas.

(3) ROLLBACK. The protocol sets CKPT_EVERY equal to the probe cadence. The ckpt.pt.prev vocabulary gap is fixed first (LOW-Q-TOK-13-PREV). Rotating N generations is owed; today there is 1. The parent checkpoint and the probe set are frozen ANCHORS: snapshots, not the live system.

(4) GATE (owed). EVAL.holdout_probe, first as telemetry (04 SR0), then as a gate: per-area worst-case bits/byte, a recovery window of 2 readings before any rollback, and rollback to the last accepted checkpoint. Weight interpolation toward the anchor is an arm.

(5) PER-STEP DAMAGE BOUND. The launcher sets OPT_GRAD_CLIP to the parent's recorded opt.grad_norm.p99; grad_norms travel in OPT's checkpoint state. No new lever.

(6) MEMORY-FIRST CHANNEL. MEM.read and MEM.blend into prediction are deferred (P5), so today the store never enters predictions. Build blend behind a MEM lever, default OFF until measured. Source quarantine before weight promotion is owed.

(7) TRUST. Source tags and DATA_TRUST 'observe' (04). MEM_SRC_SHARE 0.5 exists for memory; a per-source cap on the weight-update share is owed. Self-regulated focus is gated by trust.

(8) PLASTICITY ARMS (owed). OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY {0, 0.01} and L2-to-init, read on a plasticity probe (new-area bits/byte after N windows). Defaults unchanged.

T0 (test-time training with reset) is recorded as owed and not built.

rulings.why_B: This is B's mode itself. It follows the evidence ranking: the cheapest reversible channel first (memory, once wired), dense updates only with replay and a no-end-date schedule, gates with a recovery window (the stability gap), and frozen snapshots as rollback anchors.
rulings.why_A: The owner's route to A, 'with B we can add A later', is a continuation run: a new modality area arrives after training. It needs an LR that can rise, which the tree lacks by design (the attenuation), plus text replay (03 row 9: 0.3) and the gate. The protocol is area-based, so media areas enter it unchanged.
rulings.flexibility: The learner never cools and nothing live is frozen. Flexibility is made safe by replay, gates, the clip and rollback rather than by freezing.
rulings.unreliability_belief: Deployment input is the canonical 'unreliable system'. Honoured where supported: form 1 (varied inputs) and form 3 (mapping variability with memory and diversity), so the protocol keeps inputs varied and memory available. NOT relied on where contradicted: form 4 (unreliable targets or sources without attribution). In-tree, credibility did not emerge untagged, and learning-progress focus amplified the liar at 4 of 5 seeds; in the literature about 250 documents backdoor a model. So content and sources are gated by trust and tags. Falsifier: U-series families (f) and (g) run inside the continue protocol, trust gate off vs on.
rulings.risk: Poisoning, forgetting, and the plateau pathology (the pilots' upward turn at a constant 2e-3). Guards: parent replay, the recovery-window gate, rollback generations, the p99 clip, per-source caps, trust-gated focus. Residual: until MEM.blend and the probe land, the protocol has no memory channel and no automatic gate.

The owner's 2026-09-24 fleet (EXP=world) streamed 20M bytes and stopped at 20k windows of a roughly 105,820-window cosine, so its LR was about 0.92 of peak at the stop (arithmetic, not read from logs). rulings.group_notes:
Group: tree_and_training. Every finding below was checked this session by reading code (no training runs). Scratch: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/dec/rule_tree_and_training/horizon_probe.py.

FINDINGS THAT CUT ACROSS DECISIONS
1. The learning rate after training is decided by accident.
   - A resume at a longer run length, from a parent that carries a Q-OPT-10 revision log (any run where an S0b act fired), stays at the floor for every later step: 0.0500 of peak.
   - The same resume from a parent with no log jumps in one step, with no ramp, to about 0.54 of peak (the probe) or 0.607 (the tree's own measurement in the opt/api.py load_state docstring, a 12.1x jump).
   - The tree has no designed mechanism that raises the LR. OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM only attenuates: it multiplies the rate down.
   - So "add A later through B" currently depends on whether the parent's tokenizer acted. FRAME-POST-TRAINING rules a continuation schedule with no end date.
2. No rollback generation can be used.
   - ckpt.pt.prev has no vocabulary file, so resuming from it is refused.
   - CKPT_BEST_KEEP cannot fire, because CKPT.Retention.consider is deferred.
   - CKPT_EVERY is 0 by default.
   - This is why LOW-Q-TOK-13-PREV is raised to first priority under B.
3. B's cheapest channel is not wired.
   - MEM.read and MEM.blend are deferred (P5), so memory never enters predictions.
   - MEM.judge is deferred, so MEM_JUDGE_FRAC does nothing at any value.
4. CAP cannot act at all. CAP.observe raises NotImplementedError. Q-CLOCK-1, Q-CAP-1, Q-CAP-2 and 03b-0b4-CAP therefore affect no run until P4.
5. The two GPU fleets ran under different LR regimes.
   - The WORLD fleet (20M bytes) stopped at 20k of about 105,820 windows, with the LR at about 0.92 of peak (arithmetic).
   - The retok fleet reads a whole epoch and anneals fully.
   - The WORLD fleet's archived curves are close to the constant-2e-3 regime in which the old pilots turned upward, so part of Q-OPT-3 may already be answerable from the owner's archive.
6. Culls and merges become live.
   - At the owner's 20k windows the mean uage per expert is about 78, above FAB_GRACE 48.
   - So the utilization cull, merge and rescue can fire in owner-shape runs, and in any life after training. They are forgetting risks and must be read against per-area retention.
7. D-A13 is closed, and was already closed at d97779d. The WORLD_FEEDBACK re-test is not blocked on it.
8. Conflicts in the S0b cadence.
   - The Levels must be built before the fleet runs.
   - At k1000, FAB growth is blacked out 40% of the time (FAB_COOLDOWN 400).
   - At k1000, every retention-probe interval from proposal 04 at EVAL_RETENTION_EVERY 1000 spans an act, and 04's R-7 rebase drops it.

CONFLICTS WITH PRINCIPLES AND OWNER RULINGS
- D2 (pure-add is the default, "for now") and 04 Q4 conflict with B's replay guard. Resolution: pure-add stays the measurement protocol; replay is on in the continue protocol.
- "Nothing frozen" conflicts with rollback anchors. Resolution: freeze snapshots only, never the live system.
- The Q-RUN-8 interim ruling (3000 fires before measurement) sits against B's rule of gating before a default. It is kept as the owner's ruling, and dependent experiments pin the cadence.
- "Performance decides" conflicts with plasticity: for B, performance must be read after further learning.
- The literature digest maps OPT_LR_SHIFT_WARM to Ibrahim's re-warm. That is a terminology error.

SUGGESTED ORDER FOR B
1. Rotate the vocabulary file with the .prev checkpoint, and add its test.
2. Build the per-byte competence level for DOM. MEM's rescaled surprise follows once Q-MEM-14 is written.
3. Run the retok fleet. OPT_HORIZON_REVISE can be an optional fifth arm.
4. Build SR0: the holdout probe as telemetry.
5. Build the continue protocol:
   - a plateau schedule;
   - DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT;
   - a clip at the parent's p99 gradient norm;
   - CKPT_EVERY set;
   - rotating generations.
6. Turn the probe into a gate with a recovery window.
7. Add MEM.blend as an arm.
8. Add the plasticity arms.
The low-priority reporting fixes go alongside.

WHO RUNS WHAT
- CPU here:
  - S0b seeds 1-2 plus the nuisance control;
  - Levels on vs off;
  - known-answer tests: .prev rotation, M43, NORM_ONLY, saved counters, the merged report;
  - continuation arms and the Q-DATA-7 triple at toy scale;
  - the Q-OPT-3 grad-norm time series from a checkpointed run.
- Owner's GPU:
  - the retok fleet;
  - continuation and schedule arms at owner shape;
  - the Q-OPT-3 matched pair;
  - the WORLD re-test at S5.
- May already exist in the owner's 2026-09-24 archive, unread: n_live over 20k windows (Q-CAP-2), cull and past-grace counts (Q-FAB-5), per-flush curves and final grad-norm p50/p99 (Q-OPT-3).

NEW DECISIONS THE FRAME REQUIRES (surfaced here)
- N1: a continuation LR schedule with no end date (OPT_LR_SCHED 'plateau'; 'wsd' as a main-run arm).
- N2: DATA_REHEARSE_PARENT.
- N3: rotating checkpoint generations, N > 1.
- N4: a retention gate with a recovery window.
- N5: a gradient clip at the parent's p99 in the continue protocol.

rulings.ruling: Run it now, exactly as pre-registered, with every arm on one commit. Either run the whole fleet before SR0's DATA_SYNTH_HOLDOUT lands, or run the whole fleet after it; never split it across the change. Command: `EXP=retok CAL_WINDOWS=600 bash gpu_world.sh`. Stream: 3.78 MB, which is one whole epoch at WINDOWS x 189 bytes, with the window cap out of reach. Arms: k0, k3000, k1000, k0_nuis (SIG_WARMUP=801) and k0_rerun; seeds 0-2, auto-filled with more seeds. The primary rule is unchanged. M = max over seeds of |k0 - k0_nuis|. A cadence ships if (arm - k0) <= M at every seed; among those, the lower mean wins; if none passes, TOK_RETOK_EVERY ships 0. Shipping 0 changes only the training-run default; the act stays built and live for resume and AUD, so no functionality is removed. Interim default: TOK_RETOK_EVERY stays 3000 (ON). Since S0b, it already fires an act every 3000 windows at the owner's run length. Three B additions, pre-registered before the run; none of them changes the ship rule. (1) Keep one final checkpoint per run: a per-run CKPT_DIR=$OUT/ckpt/$tag with CKPT_EVERY 0. This needs a small gpu_world.sh option, OFF by default in the script and ON for this fleet. These checkpoints let the first after-training continuation test (a child run on a new area) start from k0 and from each passing cadence. (2) Report, per arm: prequential bits/byte per phase, FAB growth and blackout share, the MEM remap share, bpt across acts, the act's share of wall time, and windows/s (see PENDING-S0b-SECONDARIES and PENDING-GPU-THROUGHPUT-REBASELINE). (3) Label the verdict B-provisional. Once SR0's EVAL.holdout_probe exists, re-read it on end-state held-out bits/byte per area: worst area, with a nuisance-pair margin built the same way, folded into 04's E2 as an arm pair. If the shipped cadence fails that re-read, revert to 0 and name the area that lost.
rulings.changed_from_current: The core is the same: run it, and --analyze applies the non-inferiority rule. What changed under the frame: (a) the sequencing is fixed: one commit, entirely before or entirely after 04-Q5's DATA_SYNTH_HOLDOUT change; (b) CAL_WINDOWS=600, so calibration includes the first FAB.manage pass at window 501; (c) the end-of-run checkpoints are kept so learning after training becomes testable; (d) the B secondaries are pre-registered; (e) the verdict is made provisional until the held-out/retention re-read. 03b already promised that re-read at P5 but did not make it a condition of shipping.
rulings.why_B: At RUN_EPOCHS=1 the act is the only way minted vocabulary ever reaches training. After training there is no epoch roll at all, so a live segmentation is a prerequisite for learning after training. The instrument, prequential bits/byte, scores every window before the model trains on it: it measures B's plasticity half, how well the model learns text it has not yet seen. At this sizing the run crosses all four phases of the generated sliding window. I verified the phase bounds with DATA.data_plan: 0.945, 1.89 and 2.835 MB at 3.78 MB. So this is the first owner fleet that goes through area arrivals and fades; the 2026-09-24 fleet stayed in phase 1. What it cannot see is forgetting. The specific B risk that live retok adds is old areas' text being segmented with merges minted from newer areas, and only the held-out re-read can see that; hence provisional. The kept checkpoints make 'keeps learning after training' measurable at owner scale for the first time.
rulings.why_A: AUD's live codec (03b) reuses the act to re-lay media, so validating it at owner scale keeps the media door open. A byte substrate with learned, swappable segmentation is on the literature's door-open path: BLT; ZeTT; 93.4% kept under non-canonical tokenisations.
rulings.flexibility: The rule tests non-inferiority, not superiority, so a tie with the frozen control goes to the live cadence: flexibility wins unless it measurably costs. Every value stays reachable (0, 1000, 3000 and anything else). Flexibility is not free, though. Every act stamps a self-inflicted shift, and each shift opens FAB's 400-window growth blackout. The upper bound on blackout is 400/K: 40% of windows at k1000, 13% at k3000. So 'more live' can mean 'less growth', and the secondaries are there to make that trade visible.
rulings.unreliability_belief: This ruling leans on the belief: the digest lists TOK_RETOK_EVERY among the rulings that do. Each act changes the segmentation under the model, which is perturbation family (a). The act is not noise, though: it re-segments with the longer merges the run itself minted. So the primary reading (R1, clean prequential) tests 'costs nothing', not 'forces generalisation'. The CPU seed-0 result is neutral: +0.0003. The same-family form of the belief is testable in this fleet. Its prediction: the per-act loss spike, measured in bits/byte, shrinks over successive acts. It is falsified at this scale if spike depth shows no downward trend at any seed. Reading it needs the per-flush bytes record (see SECONDARIES). R3, the left-out-family reading, belongs to the U-series, not this fleet. The U-series family (a) (TOK_DROPOUT levels) should reuse this harness: equal bytes plus a nuisance-pair margin.
rulings.risk: (1) A fleet split across DATA_SYNTH_HOLDOUT loses its pairing, because every synthetic stream changes. Guard: one commit, recorded in SUMMARY. (2) Shipping on prequential bits/byte could hide forgetting. Guard: the provisional label plus the held-out, worst-area re-read. (3) This fleet cannot show the act's cost at the owner's 20 MB shape, because its tails shrink from 3.78 MB to 0. Guard: that cost was measured separately today, 8.6 s per 17 MB tail on CPU. (4) Three seeds with a max-margin is a weak test. Guard: FILL adds seeds, and M is recomputed over them. (5) If neither cadence passes, 0 re-freezes segmentation for training runs. This is acceptable only because the act stays built and the post-training mode (not yet built) will need its own cadence decision.
rulings.decisive_test: The fleet itself: owed, on the owner's GPU. Its ship rule reads prequential bits/byte. Then, after SR0, the held-out end-state per-area re-read: owed, owner GPU, folded into E2. Then a continuation from the kept checkpoints on a new area (e.g. data/continual/01_rust), reading plasticity and retention: owed, owner GPU or CPU. The CPU pre-read exists for seed 0 (2.6892 vs 2.6895 bits/byte over about 760 KB); seed 1 is owed (PENDING-CPU-S0b-SEED1).
conflicts_noticed: 03b S0b says the measurements are owed 'before the default fires', but S0b made TOK_RETOK_EVERY=3000 live: the act already fires at >=3000 windows at the default. It stays live for now (the owner approved stream rebuilding on 2026-09-26; CPU k1000 read +0.0003), but it is a default that fired before its measurement.

rulings.ruling: Take the readings in three places, not one. (a) MEASURED HERE TODAY (CPU, one thread, real text from data/train, build vocab 512, dropout 0). TOK.splice of a full 17 MB tail: 8.63 s; a half tail: 4.26 s; TOK.tokenize at a view: 7.36 s. Cost is linear, about 0.5 s/MB (1 MB takes 0.53 s). At the owner's 20 MB / 20k-window shape, the tail stays about 16-17 MB at every act. So per run, k3000 costs about 6 x 8.6 = 52 s and k1000 about 19 x 8.6 = 165 s. Against the post-fix GPU rate, which is unmeasured, that is under 2% at the old late rate of 2-3 windows/s. At the 38 windows/s early/calibration rate it is +10% for k3000 and +31% for k1000. So 04 Q9's +10% line falls right at k3000. A resume replays the epoch's tokenize plus every act's splice (compose._replay_segmentation). At k1000, near the end of such a run, a resume therefore costs about 7.4 + 19 x 8.6 = 170 s, and that cost grows linearly with the number of acts. 2. Optional: a small gauge commit, counters only and checked bit-identical against the R7 fixture:

5. Two B re-reads on the owner's GPU:

   - the WORLD_FEEDBACK re-run at the whole-epoch shape, with a retention endpoint.
6. S6(b), the media forecast, at S6.

CROSS-CUTTING FINDINGS (they bear on other groups)
(a) Run shape vs phase schedule.
- The generated schedule's phase width is DATA_STREAM_BYTES / 4. I checked with DATA.data_plan: at 20 MB the bounds are 0/5/10/15/20 MB; at 3.78 MB they are 0/0.945/1.89/2.835/3.78 MB. The schedule is ((0,1),(1,2),(1,2),(2,3)).

- That was the 2026-09-24 WORLD fleet. It is also what 04 §7's GPU run shape ('about a 20 MB stream, about 20,000 windows') and the 'owner's 17 MB tail' imply. At that shape E1 shape (b)'s 'sequential fades' would never happen.
- EXP=retok's sizing (equal bytes, one whole epoch) traverses all four phases. Use it, or something equivalent, for every B experiment, and check loop.bytes_scored against the phase bounds.
- Caveat: if the owner's geometry uses a larger LM_CTX, or real text with a much higher bpt, re-check.
(b) D-A13 appears closed.

- So the caveats in Q-WORLD-10 and in 03 §0 R2 look stale, unless the owner overrode DATA_SOURCE. This bears on LOW-D-A13.
(c) The SIG-width trigger is already met.

(d) Act cost at the owner's 20 MB shape, measured here.
