The per-area guard uses NEW-02's recalibrated budget. The rest is unchanged.

(a) chained sessions with serving (i), as ruled. 'Session mode' is the versioned 'continue' preset of explicit, printed lever values, not a mode that switches defaults. Per-session replay-record segments are required. Before (b) can be built, the look-ahead draw and record compaction must exist.

(b) the plasticity probe ON as telemetry, run on a read-only side path with a bit-identity known answer. Remedies are tried in this order: L2 toward the anchor or the initial weights first (it does not erase dormant experts), then shrink-and-perturb and FAB_RESCUE, then OPT_WEIGHT_DECAY 0.01. All are read after further learning.
(a) stays the default, and lm.ctx becomes MAY_WIDEN on the GRU arm now. The extrapolating position arm must be built BEFORE any transformer-arm checkpoint is kept as a long-lived parent.
ruling_changes.why: C43: a learned absolute position table would close A's long-context door irreversibly.

issues.target: NEW-02, C04, C11, NEW-04 (the B risk budget and gate)
issues.what: The rulings define "too much" by probe noise rather than by a tolerance the owner sets. C04's family-wise recalibration and C11's split of the held-out block then widen the effective tolerance 1.6x to 3x without saying so. No power or miss-rate requirement exists anywhere. Four of NEW-04's five gate readings have no threshold and no combination rule. As a result "without risking too much" is not actually bounded.
issues.evidence:
- I recomputed the arithmetic (scratchpad/dec/critic/arith.txt). With k=2 per area, the family-wise false-rollback rate is 8.8% / 21% at 4 areas and 16.8% / 38% at 8 (normal / SE estimated from 5 seeds). This agrees with C04.
- C04's fix sets k at 2.23 / 2.49 / 2.80 (normal) or 3.47 / 4.29 / 5.56 (t, 4 df) at 4 / 8 / 20 areas.
- C11 halves each area's probe, which multiplies the SE by about 1.41. The rollback threshold becomes 3.2-3.5 full-probe SE (normal) or 4.9-6.1 (t) at 4-8 areas.
- Take a real single-area regression of 3 full-probe SE, which is 1.5x NEW-02's own k=2 budget. The gate catches it only 46% of the time at 4 areas, 36% at 8 and 25% at 20 (normal case).
- NEW-02's validation has a pass line only for false rollbacks (at most 5%). Harmful sessions promoted are 'reported' with no pass line.
- 04-6.2 already calls 6 windows per area noisy; C11 cuts each half to 3.
- NEW-04's other readings (negative flips, KL to the anchor, the plasticity probe, canaries) have no thresholds.
- 04-Q1's margin of 0.05 b/B is 'the toy's minimum detectable effect', which is again a margin taken from noise. C04 then turns every experiment margin into this noise-derived budget.
- The tree already does this the right way round in one place: 03b-16.25 says 'raise n if the paired SE exceeds AUD_RATE_TOL / 2'.
issues.fix:
- Ask the owner for an absolute per-area tolerance ε (bits/byte per session) and a cumulative creep budget. These two numbers are what he means by 'too much'.
- Size the instrument to that tolerance: windows per area in each probe half, and seeds for the SE, such that the family-wise false-rollback rate is at most 5% AND the power to catch a regression of ε is at least 80% at the actual number of areas. This is the 03b-16.25 pattern.
- Print the achieved minimum detectable regression beside every gate verdict.
- Pre-register one combination rule. For example: a worst-area breach of ε and a canary trip are rollback triggers; KL and negative flips are alarms. Include every trigger in the nuisance calibration.
- Fix each experiment's non-inferiority margin in advance from ε, not from the SE.

issues.what: At its pre-registered owner shape, E1 never leaves phase 1 of the generated schedule. No area fades, so 'planned', 'replay' and 'retention' can differ only by the cost of the probe. The rulings amend E1 in six ways and never fix this. Two pieces of their own arithmetic are false at that shape.
issues.evidence:
- docs/proposals/04_SELF_REGULATION.md:1453 sets the run shape: 'about a 20 MB stream, about 20,000 windows'.
- A window holds about 189 bytes. gpu_world.sh:79 sizes EXP=retok at WINDOWS×189, and results/gpu_world_2026-09-24/ANALYSIS.txt shows the 20,000-window runs.
- Phases split the stream's bytes into equal parts. The retok ruling verified bounds of 0.945 / 1.89 / 2.835 MB at 3.78 MB.
- So at 20 MB each phase is 5 MB, and a run of 20,000 windows reads about 3.8-4 MB: phase 1 only.
- PENDING-WORLD_FEEDBACK noticed this and deferred it to 'another ruling group'. No ruling picks it up.
- 04-6.2's 'at least 5 readings per phase at 20,000 windows and 4 phases' assumes the phases are traversed, and so does 04-Q1's 'eng is unprotected for 75% of the run'.
- E1 costs 75 + 25 + 20 = 120 GPU runs.
issues.fix:
- Size every E-series and U-series run the way EXP=retok is sized: DATA_STREAM_BYTES = WINDOWS × measured bytes per window, one whole epoch, window cap out of reach.
- Put DATA.data_plan's phase bounds into each pre-registration, with a check after the run that every phase was entered. A run that ends in phase 1 is reported INVALID, not as a tie.
- Recompute 04-6.2's readings-per-phase floor and 04-Q1's exposure claims at the corrected shape.

issues.target: NEW-05 / C01 / FRAME (1), with C42, C05 and NEW-07
issues.what: The 'floor' continuation rate (0.05 of peak) becomes the lever default on both paths. It was chosen on R1 without any measurement. As a lever default it covers every resume, not just the continue preset, so it silently changes the LR regime of D2's add-an-area measurement protocol. Other defaults stack on top of it: a clip at the parent's p99, a quarantine delay, and promotion from owner-trusted origins only until SR6 passes. Together they may produce a learner that barely learns in its weights, which C2 forbids. No consolidation-session LR is specified.
issues.evidence:
- The tree documents the no-log re-pricing as deliberate, not an accident:
  - src/opt/api.py load_state: 'REPORTED, NEVER REFUSED: resuming at a different run length is legitimate';
  - its docstring near line 1385: 'The rate change is legitimate'.
- The Q-DATA-7 pair (+0.444 pure against +0.046 rehearsed, docs/04_CONTRACT.md:1989) reads across a run boundary. At the floor, a pure-add child forgets less because it learns less, so D2's 'architecture's own retention' headline becomes confounded by LR.
- The floor's only support is INV-28, which is confounded: old tree, constant 2e-3, no warmup.
- NEW-07 promotes quarantined material 'in a later consolidation session' at an unstated LR, while MEM retention is unproven (-0.111, n=1).
- The guard against a freeze (C26) relies on the flawed plasticity ratio described in the next issue.
issues.fix:
- Give OPT_LR_CONTINUE a value only in the continue preset. Keep today's pricing for training-run and measurement resumes, or pin it explicitly in D2 and Q-DATA-7 labels.
- Choose the preset value after C01's CPU arms, which are cheap. Read plateau and rewarm on cooled branches.
- Specify the consolidation session: its LR, replay share and gate.
- Tell the owner that 'floor' lowers the default post-training plasticity about 12x compared with today's no-log path, and let him rule on that downgrade.

issues.what: The plasticity ratio is defined the wrong way round and against the wrong baseline, so it cannot detect a freeze. Yet it is the only guard the rulings rely on to show that the budget has not turned into a freeze.
issues.evidence:
- NEW-11 defines the ratio as 'new-area bits/byte after N windows at session k, over the same at session 1'. A remedy is adopted 'if it keeps the ratio at 0.9 or above where (a) decays'.
- Lower bits/byte is better, so decaying plasticity pushes the ratio above 1, and ≥0.9 is passed.
- The baseline is session 1 under the same preset. A preset that is near-frozen from session 1 (floor LR plus the p99 clip) scores about 1.0.
- C26 names this probe (≥0.9 of session 1) as the guard against the budget turning into a freeze.
issues.fix:
- Define plasticity as a gain: the drop in bits/byte on a fresh area over N windows.
- Normalise it by the same probe run on the parent at the training-run LR, and report it beside a fresh-initialised model of equal size.
- Guard: the preset's gain must be at least a declared fraction of the parent's reference gain. Track decay as a separate trend across sessions.

critic.verdict:
The rulings are sound with fixes, but not adoptable as written. Two issues block adoption and ten are major.

**What holds up.**
- Most cited numbers check out against the tree and the evidence. I verified:
  - the FAB_LR_OWN peak-built envelope and its 4.0x clamp on the applied rate;
  - FAB's 400-window blackout after every stamp;
  - the restart sentinel (0 = one cycle);
  - load_state's continuation pricing;
  - the d2 tag numbers (C18 and C19 are correct; the digest misquoted);
  - 04's liar shares;
  - the stage-3 held-out-combination readings;
  - 03 §9's replay numbers;
  - the GPU fleet's last-half statistics.
- The owner's belief is not treated as established: C19-C23 handle it honestly.
- 'Freeze snapshots, not the live system' is applied consistently.

**What blocks adoption.**
- B's core guard is not bounded. The risk budget is defined, and then recalibrated, by the probe's noise, with no power requirement. After C04 and C11 a regression 1.5x the original budget is caught only 25-46% of the time. 'Without risking too much' therefore has no working bound.
- E1, the flagship B experiment for the draw (120 GPU runs), never leaves phase 1 at its pre-registered owner shape. It would measure nothing about retention.

**Pattern across the major issues: safety defaults chosen without measurement.** The continue preset stacks guards chosen on R1 with no evidence: the floor LR, the p99 clip, the quarantine delay, and promotion from owner-trusted origins only. The only guard against that stack freezing the learner is a plasticity ratio that is inverted and has the wrong baseline. The floor rule also silently changes the LR regime of D2's measurement protocol.

**Pattern across the major issues: owner decisions taken for him.** The priority order was written for the owner, not put to him. It ranks A-openness above flexibility, which the owner named as his means to B, and it is applied differently to tests. The belief's scope is narrowed to 'inputs', so system-level unreliability, the literal reading, goes untested. Several other owner-level choices were made silently.

**Where A is quietly favoured, or a test cannot fail.**
- A over B: tag dropout 0.25 trades tagged retention for untagged use (3 of 3 seeds); lm.ctx is widened now on B's resume path.
- A test that cannot fail: the retok fleet's spike-shrink test.

**Fix before adoption.**
- Get ε and the creep budget from the owner, and size probes to reach power at ε.
- Re-size the E-series and U-series streams so every phase is traversed.
- Scope the floor rule to the continue preset and choose its value after C01's CPU arms.
- Redefine plasticity as a gain against an absolute reference.
- Add the whole-architecture ablation and a system-unreliability family.
- Put the owner-rules register in front of the owner.

I've written the decision register at:

/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-LLM-Test/e880caf7-1208-58de-93fd-49c41549bf70/scratchpad/dec/DECISIONS.md

It is 1,204 lines (about 31,800 words, 197 KB). It follows the nine-part structure requested, plus three appendices: the critic's fixes, the defaults of new levers, and sources. It rules on all 103 inventory items and all 45 conflicts, and has 19 new decisions: the gap finder's 16 plus three the critic asked for (NEW-17 whole-architecture ablation, NEW-18 consolidation session, NEW-19 re-checking toy-set defaults). A script confirmed every ID has a row and every table has consistent columns. The part files are in `dec/parts/`.

**Critic's fixes.** All 23 are applied; none was rejected. Two were applied with an amendment, explained in Appendix A:
- **Blocking 1:** "too much" is now an owner-set tolerance ε plus a cumulative creep budget, and the probes are sized to it (at most 5% false rollbacks across areas, at least 80% chance of catching a regression of ε). The register also gives a starting value (ε 0.05 and creep 0.10 bits/byte) so it can be used before the owner rules.
- **Major, owner decisions:** there is now a register of 15 decisions only the owner can make (§3.3, O1–O15). The priority order is changed there as the critic's point implies (flexibility that serves B ranks above keeping A open), and the conflicts role's original order is offered as the alternative.

**Corrections I made while merging:**

**Unresolved:**
